task_1.title: Publish the changelog in the documentation
task_1.description: Version 2.0.1 makes the project changelog part of the published documentation so users can access release history from the docs. The provided code diff is empty, so this update does not indicate any runtime, API, or behavioral change in the library itself.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the published documentation includes the library changelog so users can review release history and version-to-version changes directly from the docs.

expectation.grounded: The 2.0.1 update should expose the changelog in the documentation set. Based on the release note and the absence of code changes in the provided diff, no public runtime API, exception behavior, or library execution semantics should change as part of this release.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to find the project's changelog in the official documentation, and upgrading to 2.0.1 should not alter how the library behaves at runtime.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce observable runtime changes, new public APIs, modified return values, different warning or error behavior, or compatibility-impacting behavior as part of this documentation update.
constraints.conceptual: This release should improve documentation discoverability only and remain behaviorally neutral for existing library consumers.

behavior: The published documentation includes the project changelog as part of the documentation content.
The changelog is available in a documentation-compatible format for inclusion in the docs build.
No runtime or public API behavior changes are evidenced by the provided code diff for this release.
acceptance_criteria: When a user views the published documentation for version 2.0.1, the changelog should be accessible from the documentation content.
When a user upgrades from 2.0.0 to 2.0.1, existing runtime behavior and public API usage should remain unchanged.
The release should communicate version history through documentation without introducing new observable execution-time effects.

task_2.title: Normalize from_jwk() input handling across algorithms
task_2.description: The 2.0.1 update fixes inconsistent JWK loading so applications can import keys through from_jwk() using either JSON text or an already-parsed object across supported algorithms. It also standardizes invalid JWK input handling so malformed or unsupported payload types raise the library's key validation error instead of surfacing inconsistent parsing failures.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that JWK-based key loading via from_jwk() works consistently for all supported algorithms when a caller provides either a JSON string or a parsed JWK object, and ensure that invalid JWK payloads fail with the library's key validation error rather than unexpected parsing or type errors.

expectation.grounded: The from_jwk() API should accept both a JSON string and a dict-like JWK payload for HMACAlgorithm and the cryptography-backed algorithm implementations covered by the shared fix. When the input is malformed JSON or an unsupported input type, from_jwk() should raise InvalidKeyError. After parsing succeeds, existing algorithm-specific key validation, such as rejecting a non-oct JWK for HMAC, should continue to apply.
expectation.conceptual: Applications upgrading to 2.0.1 should be able to pass JWK data to from_jwk() in either serialized or already-decoded form without algorithm-specific inconsistencies. Invalid JWK content should be reported as a normal key-validation failure, while valid keys should continue to be accepted or rejected according to the target algorithm's documented key type rules.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress valid JSON-string JWK handling. Do not broaden accepted key semantics beyond allowing dict input in addition to string input. Preserve existing algorithm-specific key type checks and keep invalid JWK parsing/type failures surfaced as InvalidKeyError.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should improve input compatibility and error consistency only. It should not change which keys are considered valid for a given algorithm or alter successful behavior for existing valid JWK inputs.

behavior: from_jwk() accepts a JWK supplied either as a JSON string or as an already-parsed mapping for the affected algorithms.
Passing a malformed JSON string to from_jwk() results in InvalidKeyError rather than a lower-level parsing failure.
Passing a non-string, non-mapping JWK payload to from_jwk() results in InvalidKeyError.
After input parsing, existing algorithm-specific JWK validation still determines whether the key is accepted for that algorithm.
acceptance_criteria: When an application passes a valid JWK as JSON text to from_jwk(), it should continue to produce the same usable key object as before.
When an application passes the same valid JWK as an already-parsed object to from_jwk(), it should be accepted consistently for supported algorithms.
When from_jwk() receives malformed JSON input, it should raise InvalidKeyError.
When from_jwk() receives an unsupported payload type such as a non-string, non-mapping object, it should raise InvalidKeyError.
When a parsed JWK does not match the algorithm's required key type, from_jwk() should still reject it according to the algorithm's existing validation rules.
